1.explanation:
• UIShell/README.md & UIShell/UIShell.mdx: Provide the overall implementation and Storybook usage of the SideNav Rail variant where this bug manifests.
• Dropdown/Dropdown.mdx & Dropdown/docs/overview.mdx: Explain the Dropdown component’s API, event handling, and portal behavior that the SideNav uses to render its submenu.
• MenuButton/MenuButton.mdx & MenuButton/docs/overview.mdx: Detail the pattern for a button-triggered menu (the likely mechanism driving the submenu in the rail) and how focus/hover events control open/close, critical for reproducing and fixing the hover/leave mismatch in the collapsed rail context.
1.bug_scenario:
In the SideNav Rail variant (collapsed state showing only icons), when you hover an icon that has a nested menu, the submenu panel (a Carbon Dropdown or MenuButton menu) opens. As soon as the mouse leaves the rail, the rail retracts back to its icon-only state, but the submenu panel remains rendered and floating against the page. Visually you end up with a standalone popup menu unanchored to its control, causing overlap with the page background and broken interaction flows.

Key UI elements involved:
- The UIShell SideNav Rail container (collapsed nav bar)
- The icon button or menu trigger within the rail (MenuButton or DropdownToggle)
- The Dropdown (or MenuButton) submenu panel (menu list)
- Mouse events (hover/leave) on the rail vs on the menu panel
